name: SCRB Bihar public FIR repository (View FIR)
publisher: State Crime Records Bureau, Bihar Police
caveats: UNFETCHED: *.gov.in blocked by sandbox egress policy; behaviour inferred from search-index snippets

Systematic exclusions by design: FIRs debarred by court order, FIRs touching national security, and FIRs that 'may adversely affect Law and Order and communal situations' are NOT uploaded - this censors exactly the categories a safety map most wants
ASPX postback form: results almost certainly require selecting district + police station + date range, so there is no single bulk endpoint
FIR text is Hindi/Devanagari and frequently a scanned image PDF, so geocoding needs OCR plus address parsing
An FIR is a report, not a finding - no outcome, no conviction, and withdrawn/false cases are not retracted from the page
Volume scraping of a state FIR repository has obvious privacy and defamation exposure: FIRs name accused persons who are not convicted
evidence: Two indexed endpoints under scrb.bihar.gov.in titled 'FIR -.:: Official Webiste of State Crime Records Bureau Bihar ::.' and '.:: Official Website of State Crime Record Bureau Bihar ::.'. Index snippet states that per Supreme Court and High Court orders all FIRs are uploaded except the debarred categories.
how_to_obtain: Drive the ASPX form from an Indian IP with a session (ViewState/EventValidation must be replayed). Enumerate district and police-station dropdown values first, then iterate dates. Rate-limit hard and check robots.txt before Phase 2.
notes: This is the finest-grained published record series found anywhere in the 12 states: individual FIRs attributable to a named police station, refreshed daily. It is the single strongest candidate for a police.uk-style Bihar layer, and simultaneously the biggest legal risk in this dossier.

name: West Bengal state crime statistics - NEGATIVE FINDING, RTI route
publisher: State Crime Records Bureau, West Bengal Police
caveats: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE FINDING: West Bengal is the largest state in this scope and appears to publish NO standalone state crime-statistics volume. Searches for an annual administrative or crime report on wbpolice.gov.in returned only organisation/functions and gazette PDFs.
WB SCRB's described role is to prepare CII and ADSI returns FOR NCRB, i.e. the data exists internally and is transmitted upward but is not separately disclosed to the public
Consequence: for WB, NCRB 'Crime in India' is effectively the only published source, capping granularity at district and cadence at annual with a 12-18 month lag
Cannot be ruled out absolutely - the sandbox could not fetch wbpolice.gov.in, and a Publications menu may exist that the index did not surface
evidence: Two targeted searches ('crime statistics district police station list' and 'annual administrative report PDF') over wbpolice.gov.in surfaced only Abou2019350001.pdf, Abou2021350002.pdf, Poli2019040039.pdf and Publ2022290006.pdf - none of which are crime-statistics titles. No 'Crime in West Bengal' analogue to 'Crime in Bihar' exists in the index.
how_to_obtain: RTI under s.6(1) RTI Act 2005 to PIO, State Crime Records Bureau, West Bengal Police, Bhabani Bhawan, Alipore, Kolkata 700027. Ask specifically for the district-wise and police-station-wise crime statement in the format already compiled for NCRB CII returns for the last 5 calendar years, in soft copy. Citing the existing NCRB return format is important: it makes the data 'held in the form sought' and blocks a s.7(9) refusal.
notes: Parallel RTI to Kolkata Police PIO (separate force, separate PIO) is required for the city.

name: Sikkim Police Monthly Crime Review
publisher: Police Department, Government of Sikkim
caveats: UNFETCHED: *.gov.in egress-blocked; granularity recorded as district is INFERRED from Sikkim's 4-6 district structure and is not confirmed - it may be state-total only, which would drop this to geo_granularity state

name: NCRB reporting reliability for North East states - caveat dossier
publisher: Various (ORF, CJP, FACTLY, Morung Express, Eastern Mirror, Assam Tribune)
caveats: NOT FETCHED - recorded from search-result snippets after the web-search budget was exhausted. These are commentary sources and should be read before being cited.
The substance is itself a caveat, not data
evidence: Search snippets from ORF ('Measuring Crime in India: The Limits of Statistical Compilation'), CJP ('Counting Crimes, Discounting Justice: The NCRB's statistical blind spots'), FACTLY, Morung Express ('Statistically, Nagaland remains safest for women'), Assam Tribune ('Nagaland records 28% rise in total crimes from 2021 to 2023: NCRB') and an arXiv paper (2112.07314) on NCRB limitations in rural India.
how_to_obtain: Open-download.
notes: ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S NCRB-RELIABILITY QUESTION. Documented gaps: (1) NCRB does no independent review and conducts no primary research - it compiles what states send. (2) Only COGNIZABLE crimes are counted; non-cognizable offences are excluded entirely. (3) The principal-offence rule keeps only the most serious head per FIR, systematically deflating lesser heads. (4) NE states' low reported rates are an artefact of reporting, not safety: Nagaland's Women Helpline 181 logged 2,00,000+ calls since 2016 against ~3,400 formal cases - a conversion rate near 1.7%. (5) Manipur 2023 shows a 3,399-vs-1 case jump in a conflict category, a discontinuity that breaks any trend line. (6) Insurgency-related violence in AFSPA areas routes to MHA, not NCRB. CONCLUSION: NE states DO report to NCRB, and the data arrives - but low NE crime rates must NEVER be rendered on our map as 'safe' without an explicit reporting-rate caveat. This is the single most important lawyering point in this dossier.

name: Indiastat - state crime and law statistics (commercial aggregator)
publisher: Datanet India Pvt Ltd
geo_coverage: all 12 states in scope, district cuts available
caveats: NOT FETCHED - paywalled aggregator

DERIVATIVE: Indiastat repackages NCRB and state statistical-handbook data. It adds convenience and back-series depth, NOT new information. Every NCRB caveat (principal offence rule, cognizable-only, reporting gaps) passes straight through.
Licence explicitly restricts redistribution - we could use it to validate our pipeline but almost certainly CANNOT republish its tables on a public map. Get legal sign-off before any use.
Multiple sibling domains (indiastat.com, indiastatmizoram.com, indiastatdistricteconomy.com, indiastatdistrictenviron.com) fragment the same catalogue
evidence: Indiastat crime-and-law pages surfaced in searches for every one of the 12 states (Bihar, Jharkhand, WB, Odisha, Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland variants), including district-level 'IPC Crimes - Data Statistics of All Districts' pages for Jharkhand and Mizoram.
how_to_obtain: Paid subscription from Datanet India. Negotiate redistribution rights explicitly if it is to feed a public map.
notes: Useful as a VALIDATION SET and as a cheap way to discover which district series exist before spending RTI effort. Not a primary source and not publishable as-is.

name: RTI route for the states with no usable published crime data
publisher: State Crime Records Bureaux (Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, West Bengal)
geo_coverage: Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, West Bengal
caveats: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE FINDING for these four states: no maintained, granular, published crime-statistics series was located. West Bengal publishes none at all; Manipur's is an assembly administrative report; Arunachal's is a page of unknown content; Nagaland's confirmed series stops at 2015.
RTI responses are per-state, one-off, and arrive as PDF or scanned paper - they do not give you a refreshing feed, so they cannot sustain a live map, only a baseline

s.7(9) RTI Act lets a PIO refuse to create data in a new format. ALWAYS ask for data 'in the form in which it is already held', e.g. the monthly crime return or the NCRB CII proforma, never 'please compile a table for me'.
s.8(1)(g)/(h) exemptions are routinely and often wrongly invoked for police data, especially in AFSPA states - budget for first appeals
Non-residents can file; fee is Rs 10, payable by IPO/DD/online via rtionline.gov.in for central bodies, but STATE police PIOs usually require the state RTI channel, not the central portal
evidence: Derived from the absence of results across targeted searches for each state rather than from any single document. Recorded as a negative finding per the research contract.
how_to_obtain: File parallel RTIs: (1) PIO, SCRB West Bengal, Bhabani Bhawan, Alipore, Kolkata 700027; (2) PIO, Kolkata Police, 18 Lalbazar Street, Kolkata 700001; (3) PIO, SCRB Manipur, PHQ Imphal; (4) PIO, Arunachal Pradesh Police HQ, Itanagar; (5) PIO, SCRB Nagaland, PHQ, P.R. Hill, Kohima 797001 (scrb-ngl@nic.in). Standard wording: 'a soft copy of the police-station-wise monthly crime statement for the calendar years 2020 to 2025, in the format already compiled by this office for the NCRB Crime in India returns'.
notes: BEFORE SPENDING RTI EFFORT, exhaust the legislative-assembly route. The Manipur finding (assembly.mn.gov.in administrative reports) shows that tabled departmental reports and assembly question answers are already public, already contain figures, and cost nothing. Check assembly.<state>.gov.in for all four states first.
